solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Perturbedly pan press and paparazzi, perhaps

indicators.note: something perturbed is thrown into disorder, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter as raw material

explanation.surface: Critics nervously slate both the newspapers and the celebrity photographers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' looks like a verb meaning criticise, but its letters join those of press as the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappers is slang for photographers, and paparazzi are one example of such cameramen, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: English coach upset about players in 2nd division in India?

indicators.note: about means going around, so it wraps the next piece
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: the players in a show are its cast

explanation.surface: An English manager is unhappy with his team in India's second division.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a football league table; the division is social, a subdivision of a caste.
explanation.definitionFit: The caste system is a division of Indian society, and a subcaste is a smaller, second-level grouping within one.

clue.text: Those who'll sell a lot of stuff to a nice user

indicators.note: to stuff something is to cram it in roughly, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Dealers who will sell plenty of goods to a pleasant customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of stuff' reads as quantity, but a lot is a single item at a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Auctioneers sell items called lots to the highest bidder at an auction sale.

clue.text: High Barnet is a dump with poor in an awful state

indicators.note: in an awful state means in a mess, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A complaint that High Barnet, a London suburb, is a squalid place full of poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: High Barnet is a real north London district, but barnet is Cockney rhyming slang (Barnet Fair) for hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a hairstyle swept up high off the forehead, so it is literally tall hair.

clue.text: Knight retreating by half-obliterated hill's a wise man

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

indicators.note: half-obliterated means half of the word is wiped out

explanation.surface: A knight backs away from a half-eroded hill belonging to a sage.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism a rishi is an inspired sage or seer, one of the ancient poets of the Vedas.

clue.text: Geriatric secretary gets good man to have sex

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
a good man is a saint, abbreviated ST
'it' is an old euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: An elderly secretary persuades a virtuous fellow into bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone past it is too old to function well, an informal way of calling a person aged or decrepit.

clue.text: Fend off vicar lifting dresses in party regularly

indicators.note: to dress in clothing is to be put inside it, so one piece goes into another
regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter
lifting in a down clue sends the word upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a vicar is a reverend, abbreviated REV

explanation.surface: Fight off a clergyman who is hitching up frocks at a party now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Dresses looks like a noun the vicar is lifting; it is the verb, and lifting acts on vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert is to turn away or prevent something, so it means ward off or repel a threat.

clue.text: Useful advice: best to make love intimately at first

indicators.note: to make one thing into another means swapping a letter for a new one

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A sex guide's helpful hint: the best way to make love is intimately from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as bedroom advice; love is the O in TOP, which becomes I.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is a small piece of practical advice or a helpful hint, as in tips and tricks.

clue.text: Anger after far-right racist finally hoists flags

indicators.note: after places one piece behind another in the answer
the far right of a word is its rightmost, last letter
finally picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Fury after an extremist bigot runs up banners.
explanation.walkthrough: Far-right looks political, and flags look like banners being hoisted; flags is the verb meaning weakens.
explanation.definitionFit: When energy flags it droops and weakens, just as someone who tires loses strength and grows weary.

clue.text: Conservative in strappy footwear causes uproars

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: sandals are open shoes held on with straps

explanation.surface: A Tory wearing strappy summer shoes provokes outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a public outrage over disgraceful conduct, a commotion that causes general uproar.

clue.text: Company manifesto initially accepted by workers in suits

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken inside by the receiving word

parts.note: worker bees, so workers can be bees in crosswords

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A firm's founding statement is first approved by staff dressed in business suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In suits' looks like office clothing, but suits is the verb meaning flatters, and it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Becomes as a verb means flatters or looks good on, as a hat that becomes or suits its wearer.

clue.text: Might you say a budgie picked up for less cash?

indicators.note: asks whether this is how you would speak it, pointing to sound rather than spelling
picked up means heard, as on a radio, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: a budgie is a bird that cheeps, so it is a cheeper

explanation.surface: Would you describe a pet bird bought at a bargain price this way?
explanation.walkthrough: CHEEPER is not a dictionary word; it is coined for something that cheeps, like a budgerigar.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available at a lower price is costing less money, the comparative of inexpensive.

clue.text: Slormgorm is in state after a film like Bambi

indicators.note: in places the setter's self-reference inside the country word

parts.note: Slormgorm is the setter, so 'Slormgorm is' is I'M

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be in a mood after watching a Disney cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym, so the name plus 'is' stands for 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambi is a Disney cartoon, an animated feature, so it is an example of an animation.

clue.text: Duct leakage sailors plugged with end of toe

indicators.note: something plugged has an item stuffed into it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: end of picks the closing letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A leaking pipe is stopped up by seamen using a toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duct' suggests plumbing, but it is the tear duct of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Tears flow from the tear ducts by the eyes, so they are literally the fluid escaping from a duct.

clue.text: Scottish people primarily are drunk on brandies

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter counts
drunk suggests staggering and confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some Scots are mainly getting tipsy on brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: Aberdeen is a city in north-east Scotland, and its people are called Aberdonians.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdonians are natives or residents of Aberdeen, a Scottish city, so they are a group of Scots.

clue.text: Dance beat associated with good disco ultimately

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very last, so take the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A dance rhythm linked with a decent nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' looks like a musical rhythm; it is the verb, to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance originating in Argentina, so it names a kind of dance directly.

clue.text: Main coming with food and last of pepper and salt

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea

indicators.note: last of takes only the closing letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A main course arrives with food plus the last of the pepper and some salt.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a dinner table, but salt is the old sailor and Main is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a veteran sailor, so salt is a slang term for a seagoing person.

clue.text: Hearty stewed starter and joint served with Bud

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

parts.note: bud, short for buddy, is a friend or mate

explanation.surface: A filling stew to begin, with a roast joint and a bottle of Budweiser.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearty reads as describing a filling stew, and Bud as a beer; a hearty is a sailor, as in 'me hearties', and Bud is a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors are traditionally addressed as hearties, and a shipmate is a fellow sailor serving on the same vessel.

clue.text: Couples seen by chaps in first-class conveniences

indicators.note: seen by means placed beside, so the pieces sit next to each other
in sets one piece inside the other

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with 1 read as the letter I
to couple things is to tie them together

explanation.surface: Pairs are spotted by gentlemen in posh public toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: Conveniences is the British word for public toilets, which the surface plays on, but it simply means useful facilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenities are useful facilities or comforts of a place, like a convenience is a helpful facility.

clue.text: Biscuits or bananas?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: thin dry savoury biscuits

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a choice of snacks; bananas is the slang word for crazy, not fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names savoury wafers eaten with cheese and is also British slang for insane or wildly eccentric.

clue.text: Scruffy man rises to have close shave

indicators.note: scruffy means untidy and messy, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: the two words provide the letters

explanation.surface: An unkempt fellow gets up to give himself a close shave with a razor.
explanation.walkthrough: Close shave sounds like grooming a scruffy man, but it is the idiom for a narrow escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a narrow escape from disaster, when danger passes by with very little margin.

clue.text: At front, explosive is bloody thrown over… duck!

indicators.note: at front means each word gives only its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of explosive and is

indicators.note: thrown over means flipped end to end, so the word is read the other way

explanation.surface: A warning shout: something explosive and gory is being hurled your way, so get down!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck!' reads as a command to take cover; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck, prized for its soft down feathers, so it is one kind of duck.

clue.text: A group covering number one from Slade in benefit

indicators.note: a covering word sits over and around another, enclosing it
number one from means the first letter of the following name

explanation.surface: A band covers a Slade number one at a charity benefit gig.
explanation.walkthrough: Slade were a 1970s British glam rock band with several number one hits, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or resource, something that is an advantage or a benefit to its owner.

clue.text: Fleet in weakened state after losing first couple of frigates

indicators.note: losing means letting go of some letters, which drop out

parts.note: something fragile is weak and easily broken
the opening two letters of frigates

explanation.surface: A navy is weakened after the loss of its first two warships.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet and frigates suggest a navy; fleet is the adjective meaning swift.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means swift and nimble on one's feet, so it describes someone quick and nimble.

clue.text: Genuine effectiveness found in corporate ethics

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Real effectiveness can be discovered in a company's moral code.
explanation.definitionFit: A law or body with teeth has real power to enforce its will, so the idiom means effective force.

clue.text: One seen during awfully nice mass related to Jesus

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so one piece goes inside the other
awfully suggests badly done, so the letters are mangled into another order

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted at a terribly pleasant church service connected with Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesus is held by Christians to be the Messiah, so anything to do with him as saviour is messianic.

clue.text: German diver fixed to lose fourth place essentially

indicators.note: to lose fourth means the letter in fourth position drops out

parts.note: something fixed in place is stuck

indicators.note: essentially means at the heart, so take the central letter

explanation.surface: A German diving competitor was set to miss out on fourth place.
explanation.walkthrough: Diver suggests a sports competitor; the Stuka was a German dive-bomber of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Junkers Ju 87, called the Stuka, was a Luftwaffe dive-bomber famous for its steep screaming dives.

clue.text: Scrutinise cricket? There's pressure in that!

indicators.note: in that tells us to put the item inside the thing just mentioned

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Is cricket worth examining closely? A tense game under pressure, after all.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket wants to be the bat-and-ball game; it is the chirping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something is to examine it carefully, a direct synonym for looking it over closely.

clue.text: Port American served up with slice of Roquefort

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means brought upwards, so the letters run backwards
a slice of means just a small part, here the opening letter

explanation.surface: A glass of port for an American, presented alongside a piece of blue cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Port reads as the after-dinner wine with cheese; it is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Sur is a seaport on the coast of Oman, and also the Arabic name of Tyre in Lebanon.

clue.text: Flipping game I had to store close to backgammon and go

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over so it runs backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a common crossword game

indicators.note: to store something is to keep it inside, so one piece holds another
close to means the closing letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An irritable gamer stores a backgammon set and leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word attached to the game; it is the reversal signal. Go as a verb is the euphemism for relieving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Go is a common euphemism for relieving oneself, especially in 'need to go', which matches passing water.

clue.text: Want to oust Democrat with yen to get coarse

indicators.note: to oust is to throw out, so the named letter is removed

parts.note: a want is a lack or dearth
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A wish to remove a Democrat by bribery with yen is a crude move.
explanation.walkthrough: Want is the noun meaning shortage, not a verb of desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is crude or bawdy, unrefined and down to earth, so it describes something coarse.

clue.text: Bishop lends a helping hand to slappers, possibly

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to lend a helping hand is to assist

explanation.surface: A clergyman helps out some women of loose morals.
explanation.walkthrough: Slapper is British slang for a promiscuous woman, but here it means a player who slaps the strings, as in slap bass.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap bass is a funk technique of striking the strings, so some bass guitar players are slappers.
